method: Read every task; re-derived 25 computable expected answers in Python (all agreed with the authors), hand-verified the remaining extraction tasks, probed edited checkers with extra correct and wrong replies via lab/core.run_check, checked for duplicates within the three files and against dev.json (none found). Model was not run on these tasks.

changes.issue: Lowercase regex tolerated a ```json fence but not a bare ``` fence, although the json checker accepts both, so a correct fenced reply could fail.
changes.action: Regex prefix widened to accept either fence form.

changes.issue: "the committee's name" could defensibly be answered "Orchard" while the checker requires "Orchard Committee".
changes.action: Prompt now asks for the full two-word name as written in the memo; checks unchanged.

changes.issue: Case-sensitive regex requires lowercase item names but the prompt did not state the case.
changes.action: Prompt now says item name in lowercase as written above; checks unchanged.

changes.issue: min_words 4 was an unstated constraint; a valid 2-3 word sentence containing Plumwick would fail.
min_words 4 was unstated; a valid advert of two very short lines would fail.
changes.action: min_words lowered to 2 (line_count 2 and the kite regex still guard against empty replies).

changes.issue: min_words 9 was unstated; three valid two-word sentences containing Tobbin would fail.
Prompt forbids numbering but a numbered 3-line reply passed all checks.
changes.action: Added lines_regex rejecting lines that start with a number marker or bullet.

changes.issue: Prompt forbids numbering but numbered or bulleted lines inside the 6-9 word range passed.
changes.action: Added lines_regex rejecting lines that start with a number marker or bullet.

changes.issue: A line holding two sentences (e.g. "Frogs sing. After every rain.") passed the one-sentence-per-line rule.
changes.action: Period regex tightened to ^[^.!?]*\w\.$ so each line has exactly one terminal period.

notes: No wrong expected answers found in any of the 63 tasks.
No duplicates or near-duplicates found within the files or against dev.json; invented names Wexcombe and Pim recur across files with unrelated content and were left as is.
All content is fictional and harmless; all tasks fit their sub-theme (gen_1 strict JSON, gen_2 ordered/filtered lists, gen_3 counts in free writing).
